Calcaneus.fact: The calcaneus (; from the Latin calcaneus or calcaneum, meaning heel; pl.: calcanei or calcanea) or heel bone is a bone of the tarsus of the foot which constitutes the heel.

Calcar.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Calcar.question: The _____ was Spur of cartilage in bats.
Calcar.fact: The calcar, also called the calcaneum, is the name given to a spur of cartilage arising from inner side of ankle and running along part of outer interfemoral membrane in bats, as well as to a similar spur on the legs of some arthropods. The calcar serves to help spread the interfemoral membrane, which is part of the wing membrane between the tail and the hind legs.

Cayman Brac.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Cayman Brac.question: Its terrain is the most prominent of the three Cayman Islands due to "The Bluff", a limestone outcrop that rises steadily along the length of the island up to _____ (141 ft) above sea level at the eas
Cayman Brac.fact: Its terrain is the most prominent of the three Cayman Islands due to "The Bluff", a limestone outcrop that rises steadily along the length of the island up to 43 m (141 ft) above sea level at the eastern end.

Caïque.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Caïque.question: The _____ was Traditional Greek fishing boat.
Caïque.fact: A caïque (Greek: καΐκι, kaiki, from Ottoman Turkish: قایق, romanized: kayık) is a traditional fishing boat usually found among the waters of the Ionian or Aegean Sea, and also a light skiff used on the Bosporus. The caïque is also a typical case of positioning the widest beam far aft, with a long sharp bow.

Caïque.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Caïque.question: The bow is also known in Greek as the proura or plowri, similar to the _____ prow
Caïque.fact: The bow is also known in Greek as the proura or plowri, similar to the English prow.

Caïque.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Caïque.question: Lately, it has become a short excursion vessel, and former fishermen make money from the summer tourist trade on busy islands such as Corfu and _____
Caïque.fact: Lately, it has become a short excursion vessel, and former fishermen make money from the summer tourist trade on busy islands such as Corfu and Mykonos.

Caïque.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Caïque.question: Another feature of imperial caiques was the deck pavilion, a partition or a small kiosk for the _____
Caïque.fact: There were also imperial caïques used by the Ottoman sultans and his suite for ceremonial and daily excursion purposes. Another feature of imperial caiques was the deck pavilion, a partition or a small kiosk for the Sultan.

Caïque.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Caïque.question: Historically, a caïque was a boat of 5–_____ (16–20 ft) in length, and 1 meter (3 ft) in width, used mainly for transportation
Caïque.fact: Historically, a caïque was a boat of 5–6 meters (16–20 ft) in length, and 1 meter (3 ft) in width, used mainly for transportation.
